Ascending dispatch, successful-start flag consumption, failed-start state clearing and terminal early returns match canonical code.
Bank/sample guards lack general negative-index protection; reservation and activation are described accurately.
External send permission uses low configuration bits, complementary to script gates and separate from effect-type nibbles.
Handle, bus, override and state guards match; assigned-instance and pre-instance mutation paths remain distinct.

Channel validation, filtering and indexed default storage justify sharpening the rendered SetAuxLevelAll hypothesis to a channel-specific inferred name.
Purpose correctly separates attempts on existing records from saved defaults for future records.
